request.description: Train the first complete baseline PPO candidate with the current PI-owned recipe and retain its intermediate checkpoints for later development measurement.
request.rationale: There is no candidate or completed behavioral evidence yet. A full baseline trajectory is the most direct way to establish whether the current route produces a learnable reach-and-hold policy and to nominate complete artifacts for radius-stratified, hold-stability, branch, and control-margin measurements. Its results will determine whether the next direction should remain with the baseline, change training coverage or stabilization, or obtain simulator authority evidence.

request.description: Paired development evaluation of the two strongest non-privileged baseline checkpoints on an identical official-distribution panel.
request.rationale: Training dynamics nominate checkpoints T1:checkpoint-115712 and T1:checkpoint-120832 with equal recorded training success of 0.96, but training facts do not establish development performance and the terminal checkpoint has no privileged status. A same-seed paired evaluation compares complete artifacts while preserving radius, first-entry, hold-length, and interruption diagnostics. Outcomes will determine whether to select a baseline candidate, change coverage or stabilization, or investigate a physical control limitation.

request.candidates_and_roles: No working, best-known, or retained role has been assigned. T1:checkpoint-120832 is the stronger of the two measured artifacts at the complete-artifact comparison level, but both remain development candidates far below the goal and neither is role-assigned.
request.cumulative_resource_use: One fresh training run requested 120000 steps and completed 120832 simulator steps through rollout rounding. One paired research evaluation measured two T1 checkpoints over 160 identical development episodes each. No official assessment was requested.
request.current_goal_gap: Development evidence is 65.625% for T1:checkpoint-115712 and 68.75% for T1:checkpoint-120832 on the same 160-episode panel, leaving a large gap to 98%. The evidence indicates that most failures occur before first entry into the tolerance region: 49 of 55 failures for the earlier artifact and 42 of 50 for the later artifact had no recorded first reach. Hold completion is comparatively reliable once entry occurs, with 105 and 110 complete holds respectively.
request.current_synthesis: Observation: T1 training produced a learning trajectory whose recorded training success rose to 0.96, but development evaluation of complete artifacts was only 65.625% and 68.75%; the later artifact won 9 paired episodes versus 4, with 13 discordant episodes. Observation: the two evaluation artifacts sampled target radii from 6.17 to 19.82 cm and recorded first-entry, maximum-hold and interruption diagnostics. Interpretation: the later checkpoint is the stronger complete artifact at the candidate-comparison level, but the difference is not assigned to training duration or any mechanism. Interpretation: the dominant observed failure class is failure to reach tolerance, not failure to sustain the 100-step hold, because no-first-entry episodes account for most failures and entry generally led to a complete hold. This supports the model consequence that official coverage and learned reach basins matter. The radius-specific contribution and the roles of IK branch, reset singularity, and actuator margin remain unresolved because those diagnostics were not recorded in this evaluation.
request.decision_frontier: The unresolved decision is whether the reach deficit is primarily an official inner-radius coverage/generalization problem or a branch/singular-escape/control-authority problem. Radius-stratified outcomes from the existing artifacts or a targeted measurement would support a coverage route if failures concentrate at 6-14 cm; failures distributed by radius with branch or saturation signatures would redirect toward branch-aware control or simulator characterization. Hold diagnostics do not currently justify prioritizing memory or explicit hold phase.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal requires at least 196 successes in the official 200-episode panel. The first baseline candidate measurements are far below that level, so the campaign must improve complete episode acquisition rather than infer success from training reward.
request.next_direction_or_closure: End startup and enter goal review with the active frontier focused on reach acquisition. Prefer opening a bounded inquiry that first obtains radius-stratified and branch/angle-resolved evidence from a selected complete baseline artifact; use the result to choose between coverage-focused training and control/branch investigation.

request.description: Train a fresh PPO candidate on the full official target-radius distribution while retaining intermediate checkpoints for development measurement.
request.rationale: M2 identifies the dominant first-entry deficit as inner-radius coverage: the 42 no-entry failures have mean target radius 9.82 cm, compared with 14.36 cm for the 118 entries, and the failures are concentrated in the 6-14 cm band that the baseline recipe omitted. All entries and minimum-distance states used the same positive elbow branch, so the completed evidence supports changing training coverage before branch-aware control. The fresh full-distribution recipe directly tests whether exposing the policy to the official 6-20 cm geometry raises complete episode success toward 98%; it does not claim that coverage alone explains every failure, especially because actions reached the normalized bound in M2.

request.description: Paired official-distribution development evaluation of the full-radius candidate and the prior baseline with mechanism diagnostics.
request.rationale: M2 shows that baseline first-entry failures are concentrated in the untrained inner-radius band: the 42 no-entry failures average 9.82 cm versus 14.36 cm for 118 entries, while all no-entry minima remain on the positive branch and show no pre-entry control saturation under the prior boundary diagnostic. T2 changed the training radius to the full official 6-20 cm interval, but its training dynamics never recorded success, so that recipe result does not establish behavioral failure or coverage benefit. Measuring T2:checkpoint-120832 against T1:checkpoint-120832 on identical seeds will determine whether the intervention improves complete success and whether its radius, branch, singularity, speed, and corrected boundary-control signatures support retaining the coverage route or redirecting to control/branch work.

request.outcome: Completed evidence supports a limited mechanism conclusion. In the competent baseline T1:checkpoint-120832, the 42 no-first-entry failures had mean target radius 9.82 cm versus 14.36 cm for the 118 entries, concentrating the dominant deficit in the official inner band omitted by baseline training. Those failures all reached their minimum on the positive elbow branch, and the baseline had no branch separation sufficient to make branch choice the primary explanation. The fresh full-radius T2 recipe did not learn a competent policy: it achieved 33.75% development success versus 68.75% for T1, lost the paired comparison 16-72, and 84 of its 97 no-entry failures included pre-entry boundary commands. This establishes that the tested fresh full-radius recipe is inadequate, not that official coverage is irrelevant or that actuator authority alone is causal. The bounded answer is that inner-radius coverage is the leading explanation for the competent baseline's reach deficit, while control authority remains a coupled unresolved risk exposed by the failed T2 recipe.
request.reason: The closure condition is met because completed M2 and M3 evidence distinguishes the dominant baseline failure concentration by radius, rules out a primary branch-only explanation for the observed baseline failures, and identifies the next route. The next intervention should preserve the competent outer-workspace policy while adding official inner-radius experience through transfer or curriculum; fresh full-distribution training is not supported by T2. Saturation remains a diagnostic to retain in the next development evaluation rather than a basis for changing simulator authority without a competent-policy comparison.

request.outcome: M4 provides a bounded answer to I2. The staged transfer improved complete development success from the T1 reference's 68.75% (110/160) to 87.5% (140/160) at T3:checkpoint-70656 and 94.375% (151/160) at T3:checkpoint-120832, with paired wins of 31-1 and 41-0 respectively. The final staged artifact therefore acquired substantial inner-radius capability without evidence of substantial outer-workspace regression on the same panel. Its four no-first-entry failures included two inner-band targets at 10.66 and 10.85 cm and two outer-band targets at 17.49 and 18.35 cm. All four residual no-entry failures had 498-500 pre-entry control-saturation steps and endpoint speeds near the measured upper range, so the remaining failures are consistently saturation- and speed-linked rather than evidence against the staged-coverage route.
